chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, from a man who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The Murjuna are a people who were polytheists, so they killed the likes of Hamza and Ja'far and similar ones among the believers. Then, after that, they entered into Islam, so they affirmed the Oneness of Allah and left polytheism, but they did not believe [fully] to be among the believers. They did not believe, so Paradise is not obligatory for them; and they did not disbelieve [completely], so Hellfire is not obligatory for them. So they are in that state, hopeful for the Command of Allah.'

key_terms.الشِّرْكَ: Polytheism or associating partners with God
key_terms.الْمُرْجَوْنَ: The Murjuna, a group named for deferring judgment to Allah
key_terms.جَعْفَرٍ: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, cousin of the Prophet
key_terms.حَمْزَةَ: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, uncle of the Prophet
key_terms.لِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ: For the Command/Decree of Allah, implying deferred judgment
key_terms.مُشْرِكِينَ: Polytheists, those who associate partners with God

ai.seo_question: Who are the Murjuna and what is their spiritual status according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the historical origin of the term 'Murjuna' (those who defer judgment), linking it to early converts who killed prominent companions like Hamza and Ja'far yet lacked complete faith. In Shia theology, this status reflects an intermediate state where their ultimate fate is suspended pending Allah's decision, distinguishing them from both definitive disbelievers and true believers. This concept underscores the principle of 'Tawqif' (divine deferment) regarding those whose internal belief is uncertain.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr Al Wasity, from a man who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The hopeful ones used to be the Polytheists, so they killed the likes of Hamzaas and Ja’faras and the likes of these twoas from the Momineen. Then they, after that, entered into Al-Islam, so they accept Allahazwj only.  They gave up paganism, but did not believe’ to be among believing people.  They did not deserve paradise.  They were not in denial and a rejecting attitude to be subjected to Fire (of Hell).  They are in that condition as such that it will be up to Allahazwj to either Punish or Accept their repentance.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Hassan from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti from a man who has said the following: “

Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘Al- Murjawn were a pagan people. They murdered people like Hamza and Ja’far and similar persons from the believers. Then they accepted Islam. They accepted Allah only. They gave up paganism, but did not believe to be among believing people. They did not believe to deserve paradise. They were not in denial and a rejecting attitude to be subjected to fire (of hell). They are in that condition as such that it will be up to Allah to punish or accept their repentance.”’
